parts.technique: Histogram construction (frequency density for unequal class widths)
parts.reason: Histograms with area representing frequency are explicitly covered by S2.1.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Joint probability from two-way table
parts.reason: Calculating P(A∩B) from a table is basic probability covered by S3.1/S3.2.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Complement rule
parts.reason: P(A') = 1-P(A) is explicitly listed under S3.2 guidance.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Conditional probability
parts.reason: Directly matches the conditional probability formula and use given in S3.2.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Testing independence via P(A∩B) vs P(A)P(B)
parts.reason: S3.1 explicitly gives the independence test P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B); this is a direct application.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Normal distribution - finding standard deviation from a percentile
parts.reason: S4.2 covers use of Normal distribution to find probabilities/parameters, including solving simultaneous equations; finding sigma from a percentile is standard practice.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: Direct use of Normal distribution to find a probability, covered by S4.2.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Normal distribution - finding mean from a percentile
parts.reason: Same as (a): finding a parameter of the Normal distribution using an inverse normal calculation, covered by S4.2.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Median and interquartile range
parts.reason: Measures of central tendency and variation (median, IQR) are explicitly covered by S2.3.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Boxplot with outlier identification
parts.reason: Box and whisker plots including outliers, using a specified rule, are explicitly covered by S2.1/S2.4.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Mean calculation
parts.reason: Mean is a measure of central tendency explicitly listed in S2.3.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Interpreting skewness from mean/median/quartiles
parts.reason: S2.3/S2.4 require drawing inferences and interpretations from measures of central tendency and variation, which includes commenting on skewness.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding unknown constant in a discrete probability function using sum of probabilities = 1
parts.reason: S4.1 covers understanding and use of discrete probability distributions; finding k from normalisation is basic distribution work, not the excluded mean/variance calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: E(X) and E(X^2) of a general discrete random variable
parts.reason: Explicit exclusion S4.1: 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables is excluded'. This part directly requires E(X) and E(X^2).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Variance of a linear transformation of a discrete random variable
parts.reason: Requires Var(X), excluded by S4.1, and also uses the out-of-spec result from (b).

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Probability of sum of two independent discrete random variables taking a value, via independence
parts.reason: This uses only the probability function from part (a) (in spec) and the independence multiplication rule P(X1=a and X2=b)=P(X1=a)P(X2=b) from S3.1; it does not require E(X) or Var(X), so the S4.1 exclusion does not apply here.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Full probability distribution of the sum of two independent discrete random variables
parts.reason: Built from the in-spec part (a) distribution and independence rules (S3.1); no statement explicitly covers convolution of distributions, but the calculation only uses independence probability rules applied repeatedly, so it is reasonably within the S3.1 toolkit rather than an excluded named concept.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Probability from the derived distribution of X1+X2
parts.reason: Directly follows from the in-spec distribution built in (e) using basic summation of probabilities; consistent with S3.1.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Scatter diagram and identifying explanatory variable
parts.reason: S2.2 covers scatter diagrams and explanatory/response variables explicitly; this part does not involve regression line calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Calculating equation of least squares regression line
parts.reason: Explicit exclusion S2.2: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Deducing regression line after decoding
parts.reason: Regression line calculation, excluded by S2.2, and depends on the out-of-spec part (b).

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Interpreting regression intercept
parts.reason: Depends on the excluded regression line calculation from (b)/(c); calculations involving regression lines are excluded per S2.2.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Prediction using regression line gradient
parts.reason: Uses the regression line coefficient from the excluded part (b); regression line calculations are explicitly excluded per S2.2.
